name: 51 Pegasi b
tagline: Dimidium — the original hot Jupiter, the world that rewrote planetary science.

facts.label: Discovered
facts.value: 1995 — Mayor & Queloz, first exoplanet around a Sun-like star (Nobel 2019)

history: Dimidium broke the rules. In 1995 Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz found a Jupiter-mass world orbiting its star in four days — impossible under then-current theory, which demanded gas giants form far out. The discovery launched the exoplanet era, taught astronomers that planets migrate, and won the 2019 Nobel Prize. Dimidium likely formed beyond the snow line and spiraled inward; today it is a broiling giant, so close it is tidally locked with a day side hot enough to glow faintly. Every hot Jupiter since — thousands of them — stands in this one's shadow.
